title: Language Transformers and Meaning · Level 1
slo: Explain how a language transformer represents relationships among words.

exercises.question_text: What does attention use to assign a token representation?

options.text: Its relationships to other tokens in context
options.rationale: Attention considers how a token relates to other tokens in context. Those relationships shape its representation.
Pixel values belong to image data. Language attention uses relationships among tokens.
options.better_fit: Pixel values are relevant when processing image patches.

feedback.instructional: Attention uses token relationships, not pixels.

options.rationale: Position can contribute information, but attention is defined here by relationships among tokens. Position alone cannot capture contextual meaning.
options.better_fit: Position information can help a model distinguish ordering in a sequence.

feedback.intrinsic: The representation would omit surrounding-word relationships.
feedback.instructional: Attention depends on context between tokens.

options.rationale: Translation is an NLP task that a model may support. It is not the mechanism attention uses to assign representations.
options.better_fit: Translation is a downstream language task for a semantic language model.

feedback.intrinsic: A task outcome would replace the contextual mechanism.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Attention relies on contextual token relationships.

exercises.question_text: What can a semantic language model support? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Semantic language models support text analysis. They represent relationships among language tokens.
Translation is an NLP task. Semantic token relationships can support translation.
Language generation is an NLP task supported by semantic language models. Represented token relationships help produce meaningful language.
Pixel classification is an image-processing task. A semantic language model works with language tokens and their relationships.
options.better_fit: Use this for semantic segmentation of an image.

feedback.intrinsic: The task would shift from language to pixels.
feedback.instructional: Semantic language models support language tasks.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These are language tasks supported by semantic language models.

exercises.question_text: Tokens used in similar contexts receive more closely aligned embedding vectors than unrelated words.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This misses the role of contextual similarity.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Similar contexts produce more closely aligned embedding vectors.

exercises.question_text: A semantic language model represents token relationships by assigning pixel values to words.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This treats language as image data.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Semantic language models represent token relationships with embeddings.

exercises.explanation: Correct. It uses embedding relationships, not pixel values.

exercises.question_text: What produces transformer encoder vectors with many dimensions?

options.rationale: Transformer encoders create high-dimensional vectors through complex linear-algebra calculations. The dimensions encode contextual relationships.
Bounding boxes locate objects in images. They do not create transformer encoder embeddings.
options.better_fit: Use bounding-box calculations for object detection.

feedback.intrinsic: Vector creation would be confused with object localization.
feedback.instructional: Encoder vectors arise from linear-algebra calculations.

options.rationale: Patch extraction prepares image portions for a vision transformer. It is not the calculation that creates encoder-vector dimensions.
options.better_fit: Use patch extraction when converting an image into ViT inputs.

feedback.intrinsic: An input-preparation step would replace vector computation.
feedback.instructional: High-dimensional encoder vectors come from linear algebra.

options.rationale: Tokenization identifies language units. It does not perform the complex calculations that create high-dimensional encoder vectors.
options.better_fit: Use tokenization to prepare text for language-model processing.

feedback.intrinsic: The embedding calculation would be omitted.
feedback.instructional: Tokens become encoder vectors through linear-algebra calculations.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Encoder embeddings are produced through complex linear algebra.

exercises.question_text: Which statements about tokens and vectors are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: A token can be a word or phrase.
options.rationale: A token is a language unit such as a word or phrase. A language model represents these units.

options.text: A vector is an ordered numeric array.
options.rationale: A vector contains ordered numeric values. It represents an item in multidimensional space.

options.text: An embedding can represent semantic attributes.
options.rationale: An embedding is a vector representing semantic attributes. It can represent a token or a visual patch.

options.text: A token is a portion of image pixel values.
options.rationale: A token is a language unit. A portion of image pixels is an image patch.
options.better_fit: This describes an image patch used by a vision transformer.

feedback.intrinsic: A language unit would be confused with visual input.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Tokens are units, while vectors and embeddings are numeric representations.

exercises.question_text: Transformer encoder vectors have many dimensions that encode complex contextual relationships.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Transformer encoder vectors are high-dimensional and contextual.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Many dimensions encode complex contextual relationships.

exercises.question_text: A vector is a single language word represented by a model.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This mixes a token with its representation.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A word is a token, while a vector is numeric.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe a vision transformer? Select all that apply.

options.text: It is trained on many images.
options.rationale: A vision transformer is trained on image data. It applies the transformer approach to images.
A ViT extracts image patches from an image. Each patch contains a portion of pixel values.

options.text: It converts patches into linear vectors.
options.rationale: A vision transformer converts image patches into linear vectors. These vectors are then processed using the transformer approach.

options.text: It uses text tokens instead of image patches.
options.rationale: Text tokens are language-model inputs. A ViT begins with image patches from visual data.
options.better_fit: This fits a language transformer processing written text.

feedback.instructional: Vision transformers use patches, not text tokens.

exercises.explanation: Correct. ViTs process images as patches converted into vectors.

options.rationale: NLP stands for natural language processing. It is the AI discipline for processing and modeling language.
This is not the expansion of NLP. Prediction can be a language-model task, but NLP is the broader discipline.
options.better_fit: This phrase could loosely describe a model that predicts upcoming words.

feedback.intrinsic: The term would be expanded incorrectly.

options.rationale: This phrase refers to neither the standard acronym nor language processing. NLP concerns language rather than spatial locations.
options.better_fit: It might describe a hypothetical system for spatial-location data.

feedback.intrinsic: A language discipline would be mislabeled as a spatial task.

options.rationale: This is not the established meaning of NLP. NLP is an AI field, not a communication protocol.
options.better_fit: A protocol could govern data exchange between software systems.

feedback.intrinsic: The discipline would be confused with a technical standard.
feedback.instructional: Recall the full term: natural language processing.

exercises.question_text: A vision transformer applies the transformer approach to text tokens instead of image patches.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This routes images through language units.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A ViT applies transformers to image patches, not text tokens.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A vision transformer uses image patches.

exercises.question_text: NLP is an AI discipline focused on processing and modeling language.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: NLP processes and models natural language.

exercises.explanation: Correct. That is the focus of NLP.

flashcards.back: A word, phrase, or other language unit.
A portion of an image containing pixel values.
